title: Finance: Future Value Annuities and Sinking Funds
seo_title: Grade 12 Future Value Annuities Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems involving present value and future value annuities; make use of logarithms to calculate the value of n, the time period, in the equations A = P(1 + i)ⁿ or A = P(1 − i)ⁿ; critically analyse investment and loan options and make informed decisions as to the best option(s), including pyramid schemes.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 finance worksheets: future value annuities, sinking funds and monthly savings. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A future value annuity is equal payments that grow with interest: F = x[(1 + i)ⁿ − 1]i.
  • For monthly payments, i = annual rate ÷ 12 and n = years × 12.
  • A sinking fund saves for something in the future: future cost (inflation) − scrap value (depreciation).
  • Draw a timeline to see when payments start and stop.

Examples

Example

R500 per month, 5 years, 9% p.a. monthly

i = 0,0075, n = 60

Answer: F = R37 712,64

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
x × nThat ignores interest.
Yearly valuesMonthly: i ÷ 12 and n × 12.
The wrong formulaSaving for later uses F.

faq.a: Calculate the value of an investment or loan using future value and present value annuities, and use sinking funds.
